rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali teaches that a person's allotted provision cannot be outstripped by skill or reduced by folly, counseling trust, restraint, and reflection rather than anxious haste.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال كان أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام كثيرا ما يقول اعلموا علما يقينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Munkadir recounts that his attempt to admonish Muhammad al-Baqir for laboring in the heat was reversed by the Imam's response.
rows.anchor: حتى رأيت ابنه محمد بن علي فأردت أن أعظه فوعظني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Imam explains that working to support himself and his dependents is obedience to God; he feared dying in disobedience, not while lawfully earning.
rows.anchor: جاءني وأنا في طاعة من طاعة الله عز وجل أكف بها نفسي وعيالي

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: When questioned about exhausting himself on a very hot day, al-Sadiq says he seeks provision so he will not depend on the questioner or others.
rows.anchor: قال يا عبد الأعلى خرجت في طلب الرزق لأستغني به عن مثلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief that provision is decreed does not conflict with the command to seek it.
rows.anchor: ولا منافاه بين القضاء بالرزق وبين الأمر بطلبه

rows.speaker: أبو رزين
rows.claim: A report asks where God was before creating; the Prophet answers that He was in an 'ama, with air above and below, and that He created the Throne over water.
rows.anchor: عن أبي رزين قال قلت يا رسول الله اين كان ربنا قبل أن يخلق خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i glosses al-'ama as a cloud opaque to sight; the phrase about air may mean emptiness or, if air is literal, that this cloud was not enclosed by it.
rows.anchor: العماء الغيم الذي يمنع نفوذ البصر فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Abu Razin report can suggest corporealism, the author interprets its 'ama as a metaphor for God's unseen essence, beyond sight and bewildering minds.
rows.anchor: والرواية من أخبار التجسم ولذا وجه بأن قوله في عماء " الخ " كناية عن غيب الذات

rows.speaker: عمران بن حصين
rows.claim: In answer to Yemenites asking how things began, the Prophet says God preceded everything, His Throne was over water, and the Preserved Tablet recorded all things before the heavens and earth were made.
rows.anchor: عن عمران بن حصين قال قال أهل اليمن يا رسول الله أخبرنا عن أول هذا الأمر كيف كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A parallel version is attributed to Burayda and places the lost camel episode differently; this variation, the author says, weakens both reports.
rows.anchor: وهذا مما يوهن الحديثين

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: The Prophet glosses being tested for the best deeds as being tested for the best intellect, defining the best intellect by piety from prohibitions and knowledge of obedience.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال تلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says the test concerns the soundness of deeds, not their quantity; soundness comes from fear of God and sincere intention.
rows.anchor: ولكن أصوبكم عملا، وإنما الإصابة خشية الله والنية الصادقة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq adds that keeping a deed alive until it becomes sincere is harder than doing it, and a truly pure deed seeks praise from God alone.
rows.anchor: الإبقاء على العمل حتى يخلص أشد من العمل

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: He says intention is better than the deed and is itself the deed, explaining that action matters only through its intention and citing 17:84.
rows.anchor: والنية أفضل من العمل ألا إن النية هي العمل

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A report from al-Sadiq interprets the postponed punishment as the Qa'im's rising and the counted community as his companions, the people of Badr; the author notes parallel reports and an alternative count of 313-plus companions.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير النعماني بإسناده عن إسحاق بن عبد العزيز عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about the ship's course and anchorage may be a standalone nominal sentence meaning that its sailing and mooring are by God's name; the name may also be an insertion meaning by God.
rows.anchor: بسم الله إجراؤها وإرساؤها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Noah said 'in God's name' as the vessel began to sail and again when it came to rest.
rows.anchor: كان إذا أراد أن تجري قال بسم الله فجرت، وإذا أراد أن ترسو قال بسم الله فرست

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The author reports Mujahid's reading mujriha and mursiha as active participles in the genitive, describing God.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد مجريها ومرسيها بلفظ اسم الفاعل مجروري المحل صفتين لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawj is either a collective noun like tamr or a plural of mawja, meaning a great mass of water that rises above the rest; the wording implies the ship rode atop the water, not submerged like a fish.
rows.anchor: وهي قطعة عظيمة ترتفع عن جملة الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The son had withdrawn to a distant place; Noah's calling rather than simply speaking to him signals that separation, while the diminutive 'my son' conveys compassion.
rows.anchor: المعزل اسم مكان من العزل وقد عزل ابنه نفسه عن أبيه والمؤمنين في مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah says not to be with the unbelievers so his son will not share their punishment as he shared their company; Noah does not yet know his son is inwardly an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: ولا تكن مع الكافرين فتشاركهم في البلاء كما شاركتهم في الصحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The son expects a mountain to protect him, but Noah says no mountain or other refuge can protect anyone from God's decree of drowning, except those who take refuge in God.
rows.anchor: لا عاصم اليوم - وهو يوم اشتد غضب الله وقضى بالغرق لأهل الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wave cuts off their conversation; had it not done so, Noah would have learned his son's unbelief and disowned him.
rows.anchor: ولو لم يحل الموج بينهما ولم ينقطع الكلام بذلك لعرف كفره وتبرأ منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The setting's mountainous terrain made it easy for a person to climb one of the local mountains.
rows.anchor: إلى أن أرضهم كانت أرضا جبلية لا مؤنة زائدة في صعود الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author defines the closing commands: swallowing sends something through the throat, desisting means stopping from the outset, and the water's recession is its being drawn from the surface into the earth.
rows.anchor: البلع إجراء الشيء في الحلق إلى الجوف، والإقلاع الإمساك وترك الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A narrative has Noah plead for guidance if God still wants his people, or patience until God's judgment otherwise; God then says no more of the people will believe and commands him to build an ark of wood to cleanse the earth of sinners.
rows.anchor: فأوحى الله إليه وآيسه من إيمان قومه وأخبره أنه لم يبق في أصلاب الرجال ولا في أرحام النساء مؤمن

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq relates that the original Kufa mosque was laid out by Adam and that the flood, later Sasanians and Nu'man, and then Ziyad altered its site.
rows.anchor: إن هذا الموضع كان مسجد الكوفة الأول الذي كان خطه آدم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: The same report locates Noah's home in a village west of Kufa near the Euphrates and says Noah, a carpenter, built the first vessel to sail on water.
rows.anchor: وكان منزل نوح وقومه في قرية على منزل من الفرات مما يلي غربي الكوفة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says Noah built the ark by hand in the Kufa mosque; the two construction periods totaled eighty years, while he rejects the popular claim of five hundred years.
rows.anchor: قال في دورين. قلت وكم الدوران؟ قال ثمانين سنة.

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: The report points out where Noah's people set up Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq, and Nasr, and identifies that place with the site of a later house.
rows.anchor: وها هنا نصبت أصنام قوم نوح يغوث ويعوق ونسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author includes a long tradition as a sample of many Shi'i and Sunni reports that can help readers understand the Qur'anic narratives, although much of its material is not directly exegetical.
rows.anchor: أوردناها لتكون كالأنموذجة من روايات كثيرة وردت في هذه المعاني من طرق الشيعة وأهل السنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report's instruction to hurry the ship's construction is inferred from God's command to build it with divine oversight and revelation.
rows.anchor: وفي الرواية استفادة التعجيل في صنع السفينة من قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addition 'ibn Abi Sufyan' after Ziyad may have been supplied by a transmitter; the Imam's wording may only have been Ziyad.
rows.anchor: وفي الرواية نسبة زياد إلى أبي سفيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oven's boiling served as the promised sign of the imminent flood, as the Qur'anic sequence presents it as the appointed signal to board.
rows.anchor: وكون فوران التنور علامة له عليه السلام يعلم به اقتراب الطوفان من الوقوع واقع في عدة من روايات الخاصة والعامة

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali's report says the oven boiled in a woman's house at the appointed time; Noah sealed it, opened it to admit or release people, then removed the seal as water rose and the flood began.
rows.anchor: عن أبي رزين الأسدي عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام قال إن نوحا عليه السلام لما فرغ من السفينة وكان ميعاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reads Noah's two prayers as distinct: first, 'I am overcome, so help me' before God despaired of the people's faith; later, after that disclosure, he prayed for every unbeliever to be removed.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الرواية أن له عليه السلام دعاءين على قومه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Humran reports from al-Baqir that eight people believed with Noah; the author says other proposed totals have no evidence.
rows.anchor: وفي معاني الأخبار بإسناده عن حمران عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports giving totals of six, seven, ten, seventy-two, or eighty believers have no proof, though the author resolves the separate eight and eighty reports by supposing the remainder were Noah's family.
rows.anchor: وللناس في عددهم أقوال أخر ستة أو سبعة أو عشرة أو اثنان وسبعون أو ثمانون ولا دليل على شيء منها

rows.speaker: علي بن موسى الرضا
rows.claim: Al-Rida says Noah, his children, and followers numbered eighty at landing and founded a settlement called the Village of Eighty; al-Tabataba'i reconciles this with eight believers by counting the rest as Noah's family.
rows.anchor: قال الرضا عليه السلام لما هبط نوح إلى الأرض كان نوح وولده ومن تبعه ثمانين نفسا

rows.speaker: علي بن موسى الرضا
rows.claim: Al-Rida says Noah's son was excluded from his family because he opposed Noah's religion, while Noah counted those who followed him as family; the son was biologically his, contrary to readings making him his wife's child.
rows.anchor: عن الرضا عليه السلام قال سمعته يقول قال أبي قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام إن الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i connects the saved 'family' with all rescued companions in 21:76, and says the two reported recitations were interpreted to support an illegitimate-son reading; the Qur'an's wording does not support it, and the Torah is silent about the drowned son.
rows.anchor: أقول ولعله عليه السلام يشير بقوله { وجعل من اتبعه من أهله }

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: The author rejects the argument that Noah's son could not be his biological child because Noah invoked the promise to save his family: the promise did not say all his descendants would be saved.
rows.anchor: واستدلاله بما استدل به سخيف فإن الله وعده بنجاة أهله

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن علي
rows.claim: Al-Baqir is reported to explain 'his son' as a Tayy dialect expression for a wife's son, even though the author ultimately relies on al-Rida's report that he was Noah's biological son.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر محمد بن علي في قوله

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq likewise explains that Tayy speakers call a wife's son her son; al-Baqir is also reported as saying Noah did not know the boy's true status when he called him 'my son.'
rows.anchor: عن موسى عن العلاء بن سيابة عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قول الله

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: One report says the earth objected that it had only been commanded to swallow its own water, so rainwater remained and became a sea surrounding the world.
rows.anchor: عن أحدهما عليهما السلام قال لما قال الله { يا أرض ابلعي ماءك ويا سماء أقلعي } قالت الأرض

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن موسى
rows.claim: A report from Musa al-Kazim locates Mount Judi near Mosul, while a report from al-Sadiq places it at the Euphrates of Kufa; the author favors the former as supported by other reports.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي الحسن موسى عليه السلام في حديث ذكر فيه الجودي قال وهو جبل بالموصل

rows.speaker: عبد الحميد بن أبي الديلم
rows.claim: A report says the pronouncement against the wrongdoers was made when Noah boarded the ark.
rows.anchor: لما ركب نوح عليه السلام في السفينة قيل بعدا للقوم الظالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report in al-Majma' says Quraysh gave up their attempt to imitate the Qur'an after hearing the earth-and-sky command, recognizing no human speech could match it.
rows.anchor: فعكفوا على لباب البر ولحوم الضأن وسلاف الخمر أربعين يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an mentions Noah in roughly forty places but does not narrate his life as a complete chronological history, because its purpose is guidance; Hud gives the fullest account in verses 25–49.
rows.anchor: ذكر اسمه عليه السلام في القرآن في بضع وأربعين موضعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an cites prophetic and communal stories to show God's pattern, prompt reflection, and complete the proof; Noah's story is told in six surahs, with Hud the most detailed.
rows.anchor: وربما أشار إلى طرف من قصص الأنبياء والأمم لتظهر به سنة الله في عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity began after Adam as one simple community on its natural disposition, but pride and domination grew into idolatry, social stratification, exploitation, and conflict.
rows.anchor: كان الناس بعد آدم عليه السلام يعيشون أمة واحدة على بساطة وسذاجة، وهم على الفطرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By Noah's time corruption, abandonment of monotheism and social justice, and idol worship had spread; the named idols include Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq, and Nasr.
rows.anchor: وقد سمى الله سبحانه منها ودا وسواعا ويغوث ويعوق ونسرا سورة نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent Noah with scripture and law to call people to God's oneness, rejection of partners, and equality, through warning and good news.
rows.anchor: فبعث الله نوحا عليه السلام وأرسله إليهم بالكتاب والشريعة يدعوهم إلى توحيد الله سبحانه وخلع الأنداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's teaching included surrender to God, commanding right and forbidding wrong, prayer, justice, avoiding indecency, honesty, and honoring covenants; the Qur'an first depicts him naming God in important undertakings.
rows.anchor: كان عليه السلام يدعوهم إلى توحيد الله سبحانه ورفض الشركاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah spent 950 years among his people before seeking God's aid.
rows.anchor: لبثه في قومه لبث عليه السلام في قومه ألف سنة إلا خمسين عاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah spent 950 years calling people who mocked him, called him mad, and accused him of seeking superiority; God then said no more would believe and consoled him.
rows.anchor: لبث عليه السلام في قومه ألف سنة إلا خمسين عاما يدعوهم إلى الله سبحانه فلم يجيبوه إلا بالهزء والسخرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After God disclosed that no more of his people would believe, Noah prayed for their destruction and for the earth to be cleansed of them.
rows.anchor: فدعا عليهم بالتبار والهلاك، وأن يطهر الله الأرض منهم عن آخرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God ordered Noah to build the ark under divine care and revelation; people mocked him as he built it on dry land, and he warned that punishment would come to them.
rows.anchor: أمره الله تعالى أن يصنع الفلك بتأييده سبحانه وتسديده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the oven overflowed, God instructed Noah to bring aboard pairs of animals, his household except those condemned to drown, and the believers.
rows.anchor: حتى إذا تمت صنعة الفلك وجاء أمر الله وفار التنور أوحى الله تعالى إليه أن يحمل في السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain poured from the sky and springs burst from the earth; the flood met as decreed, lifted the ark into mountainous waves, and seized the wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: فتح الله أبواب السماء بماء منهمر وفجر الأرض عيونا فالتقى الماء على أمر قد قدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the flood, God ordered the earth to swallow the water and the sky to clear; the ark settled on Judi, and Noah landed safely with blessings and future generations.
rows.anchor: وأوحي إلى نوح عليه السلام أن اهبط إلى الأرض بسلام منا وبركات عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's son stayed outside the ark, disbelieving his father's warning and trusting a mountain; the wave separated them and drowned the son.
rows.anchor: وكان لا يصدق أباه في أن من تخلف عنها فهو غريق لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah had not known that his son concealed unbelief, unlike his knowledge of his wife; otherwise the son's fate would not have grieved him, since Noah had prayed for the unbelievers' destruction.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن نوح عليه السلام يعلم منه إبطان الكفر كما كان يعلم ذلك من امرأته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah appealed that his son belonged to his family and invoked God's promise to save his family, stopping short of a direct demand for rescue because he lacked knowledge that his son was excluded.
rows.anchor: رب إن ابني من أهلي وإن وعدك الحق وعدتني بإنجاء أهلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's answer explains that the son is not among Noah's family because he acted unrighteously, and warns Noah against asking about what he does not know.
rows.anchor: يا نوح إنه ليس من أهلك إنه عمل غير صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah responds by seeking refuge from asking without knowledge and asks for God's forgiveness and mercy, admitting he would otherwise be among the losers.
rows.anchor: رب إني أعوذ بك أن أسألك ما ليس لي به علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the Qur'an's statement that Noah's descendants were the ones who remained after the flood.
rows.anchor: وجعلنا ذريته هم الباقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is the father of the prophets mentioned in the Qur'an except Adam and Idris.
rows.anchor: وهو عليه السلام أبو الأنبياء المذكورين في القرآن ما عدا آدم وإدريس عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah first opened the way of religious law and combined rational argument with revelation; as the source of world monotheism he receives a universal salutation unmatched by another prophet.
rows.anchor: وهو عليه السلام أول من فتح باب التشريع وأتى بكتاب وشريعة وكلم الناس بمنطق العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God calls Noah chosen, good-doing, grateful, believing, and righteous.
rows.anchor: وعده من المحسنين وسماه عبدا شكورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The last prayer attributed to Noah asks forgiveness for himself, his parents, believing entrants to his house, and all believing men and women, while asking destruction for wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: رب اغفر لي ولوالدي ولمن دخل بيتي مؤمنا وللمؤمنين والمؤمنات

rows.speaker: التوراة الحالية
rows.claim: The Torah says God ordered Noah and his whole family into the ark, having judged him righteous in his generation.
rows.anchor: هكذا فعل. وقال الرب لنوح ادخل أنت وجميع بنيك إلى الفلك

rows.speaker: التوراة الحالية
rows.claim: In the Torah account, Noah obeys God's command and enters the ark with his sons, wife, and sons' wives; it specifies seven pairs of clean animals and birds but two of unclean animals.
rows.anchor: من جميع البهائم الطاهرة تأخذ معك سبعة سبعة ذكرا وانثى

rows.speaker: التوراة الحالية
rows.claim: The Torah says the water steadily receded, and the ark came to rest on Ararat.
rows.anchor: وكانت المياه تنقص نقصا متواليا إلى الشهر العاشر

rows.speaker: التوراة الحالية
rows.claim: Noah sent out a raven and then doves; an olive leaf and the dove's failure to return showed the waters had fallen.
rows.anchor: وأرسل الغراب فخرج مترددا حتى نشفت المياه عن الأرض

rows.speaker: التوراة الحالية
rows.claim: The Torah records God's covenant that a flood would never again destroy all living beings.
rows.anchor: أقيم ميثاقي معكم فلا ينقرض كل ذي جسد أيضا بمياه الطوفان

rows.speaker: التوراة الحالية
rows.claim: The rainbow is given as the sign of the covenant between God, the earth, and every living creature.
rows.anchor: وضعت قوسي في السحاب فتكون علامة ميثاق بيني وبين الأرض

rows.speaker: التوراة الحالية
rows.claim: The Torah concludes that Ham saw Noah's nakedness while Shem and Japheth covered him without looking, prompting Noah to curse Canaan and bless the other sons; Noah lived 950 years.
rows.anchor: فلما استيقظ نوح من خمره علم ما فعل به ابنه الصغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reads the Qur'an as assigning Noah 950 years of preaching before the flood, as stated in 29:14.
rows.anchor: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه فلبث فيهم ألف سنة إلا خمسين عاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah includes a rainbow covenant, raven and dove reconnaissance, and specific ark dimensions and structure absent from the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ومنها ما ذكر فيه من حديث قوس قزح وقصة إرسال الغراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says such details became common in accounts of Noah among early Muslims and largely resemble Isra'iliyyat.
rows.anchor: وقد كثر الاقتصاص بمثل هذه المعاني في قصة نوح عليه السلام في لسان الصحابة والتابعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah adds rainbow covenant details, raven and dove reconnaissance, ark dimensions and levels, and flood duration and height, details absent from the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: من حديث قوس قزح وقصة إرسال الغراب والحمامة للاستخبار وخصوصيات السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author considers some of those details improbable, especially a rainbow covenant; many such reports circulated among early Muslims and resemble Isra'iliyyat.
rows.anchor: وبعضها بعيد مستبعد كالميثاق بالقوس

rows.speaker: صاحب المنار
rows.claim: Al-Manar's author says ancient national histories contain flood narratives, some close to Genesis and others differing only slightly; he treats the Chaldean account as the closest parallel.
rows.anchor: قد ورد في تواريخ الأمم القديمة ذكر للطوفان منها الموافق لخبر سفر التكوين إلا قليلا

rows.speaker: برهوشع ويوسيفوس
rows.claim: They report that Zizustros was warned in a dream that a flood would destroy humanity and built a vessel for himself, his family, and close friends; the account also resembles Genesis in portraying corrupt giants punished by the flood.
rows.anchor: فقد نقل عنهم " برهوشع " و " يوسيفوس " أن " زيزستروس " رأى في الحلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported cuneiform tablets from Ashurbanipal's era allegedly copied a much older flood narrative, predating Genesis.
rows.anchor: وقد عثر بعض الانجليز على ألواح من الآجر نقشت فيها هذه الرواية بالحروف المسمارية

rows.speaker: أفلاطون
rows.claim: In Plato's account, Egyptian priests told Solon that floods repeatedly changed the earth and destroyed human generations and their knowledge.
rows.anchor: أن السماء أرسلت طوفانا غير وجه الأرض فهلك البشر مرارا بطرق مختلفة

rows.speaker: مانيتون
rows.claim: Manetho reportedly recorded a flood after Hermes I, himself later than Menes I; Greeks also tell of Deucalion and Pyrrha surviving a world flood.
rows.anchor: وأورد " مانيتون " خبر طوفان حدث بعد هرمس الأول

rows.speaker: الفرس القدماء
rows.claim: Ancient Persians attributed a flood to evil and Ahriman and said it began in an old woman's oven; Zoroastrians denied a worldwide flood, limiting it to Iraq and Kurdistan.
rows.anchor: وروي عن قدماء الفرس طوفان أغرق الله به الأرض بما انتشر فيها من الفساد والشرور

rows.speaker: الهنود القدماء
rows.claim: Indian tradition describes seven floods, the last saving a king and wife in a Vishnu-commanded boat; Brahmans, like Magi, deny that the flood covered all India, while flood stories also occur in Japan, China, Brazil, and Mexico.
rows.anchor: وكذا قدماء الهنود يثبتون وقوع الطوفان سبع مرات في شكل خرافي آخرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surveyed flood traditions share the idea that God punished human wrongdoing; the Avesta's version has Ahura Mazda tell Yima or Jamshid to build a protected enclosure stocked with people, animal pairs, and food-producing plants.
rows.anchor: وكل هذه الروايات تتفق في أن سبب ذلك عقاب الله للبشر بظلمهم وشرورهم

rows.speaker: الوثنيون الهنود
rows.claim: The Manu story says a rescued fish predicts a flood and tells Manu to build a ship; when the waters rise, it tows his ship by its horn to northern mountains, leaving him alone after the waters recede.
rows.anchor: والخطر العظيم المحدق الذي أنبأت به السمكة كان طوفانا سيجرف جميع المخلوقات

rows.speaker: الشيعة
rows.claim: The familiar Shi'i view is that Noah's mission was universal; reports from the Imams also say all five prophets of resolve were sent to all people.
rows.anchor: فالمعروف عند الشيعة عموم رسالته، وقد ورد من طرق أهل البيت عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: بعض أهل السنة
rows.claim: Some Sunnis argue for Noah's universal mission from the worldwide scope of the flood, Noah's prayer, the statement that his descendants survived, and a sound intercession report calling him the first messenger sent to the people of earth.
rows.anchor: وأما أهل السنة فمنهم من قال بعموم رسالته مستندا إلى ظاهر الآيات الناطقة بشمول الطوفان

rows.speaker: بعض أهل السنة
rows.claim: Other Sunnis deny a universal mission, relying on the sound hadith that each prior prophet was sent only to his own people, whereas Muhammad was sent to all people.
rows.anchor: وكان كل نبي يبعث إلى قومه خاصة وبعثت إلى الناس كافة

rows.speaker: بعض أهل السنة
rows.claim: Those denying Noah's universal mission interpret 'earth' as the homeland of his people, so his prayer and God's warning concern his own people and his surviving descendants rather than humanity everywhere.
rows.anchor: فمعنى الآية الأولى لا تذر على هذه الأرض من كافري قومي ديارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the debate has not been adequately argued and grounds prophecy in a real human need and a true relationship with God, not an arbitrary convention.
rows.anchor: والحق أن البحث لم يستوف حقه في كلامهم، والذي ينبغي أن يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A real cosmic law directs each species toward its existential perfection and end; humanity too has a good and happiness toward which individuals and society move.
rows.anchor: ناموس تكميل الأنواع وهدايتها إلى غاياتها الوجودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human flourishing requires cooperation because an individual's many needs and tasks exceed what one person can provide, while practical reason leads each person to use others' work just as others seek to use his.
rows.anchor: فالعقل العملي الذي يبعثه إلى الاستفادة من كل ما يمكنه الاستفادة منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cooperative social life is forced by needs and mutual checks, but humanity's first impulse is self-interest; the powerful therefore exploit and enslave the weak when unchecked.
rows.anchor: فهو في الحقيقة مدني تعاوني بالطبع الثاني وإلا فطبعه الأولي أن ينتفع بكل ما يتيسر له الانتفاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every society relies on customs, norms, or laws to govern cooperation; these shared ideas shape conduct and mediate between human incompleteness and fulfillment.
rows.anchor: ومن الضروري أن الاجتماع التعاوني بين الأفراد لا يتم إلا بقوانين يحكم فيها وحفاظ تقوم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's providence must guide humans toward the happiness and perfection of life, just as creation and innate faculties guide other species toward their good.
rows.anchor: وقد علم أن من الواجب في عناية الله أن يهدي الإنسان إلى سعادة حياته وكمال وجوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human nature equips people to feel what benefits them and distinguish good from evil and happiness from misery.
rows.anchor: إلى أن يشعر بما فيه نفعه ويميز خيره من شره وسعادته من شقائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine care therefore supplies foundational beliefs and practical laws that lead people to perfection; innate practical reason cannot do so alone because it drives both exploitation and conflict, and criminals also possess reason.
rows.anchor: ولا يكفي في ذلك ما جهز به الإنسان من العقل - وهو ها هنا العملي منه - فإن العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revelation is a second way to teach the true law and path to happiness: a divine communication about beliefs and conduct that bring worldly and afterlife success.
rows.anchor: فظهر أن هناك طريقا آخر لتعليم الإنسان شريعة الحق ومنهج الكمال والسعادة غير طريق التفكر والتعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says prophecy adds nothing to reason because people disobey both, and revelation has not in fact made society follow the right path.
rows.anchor: فإن العالم الإنساني لم يخضع لشرائع الأنبياء كما لم يصغ إلى نداء العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author distinguishes God's duty to provide guidance that would perfect society if followed from the empirical question whether people actually follow it; the present argument concerns the former.
rows.anchor: لهذا البحث جهتان جهة أن العناية الإلهية من واجبها أن تهدي المجتمع الإنساني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fact that most people fail to reach their species' natural end does not remove the need for prophetic guidance; without it, reason alone would not complete God's proof, since reason also serves individual self-interest.
rows.anchor: فطريق النبوة مما لا مناص منه في تربية النوع بالنظر إلى العناية الإلهية
